reasoning:
POSTCONDITION: two artifacts must exist — a transformed copy of the supplied research dataset, and a comparison of three named aggregate totals — satisfying four acceptance claims: (1) the listed direct identifiers are gone, (2) every equivalence class over the supplied quasi-identifier set has ≥5 rows, (3) each of the three named totals is within 1% of its source value and the returned comparison reports it truthfully, (4) the deliverable does not claim zero re-identification risk. A fifth, non-stated-but-implied claim carries the real gaming risk: the returned rows must actually derive from the source records, since constraints (2) and (3) are trivially satisfiable by fabricating rows.

AUTHORITIES/ORACLES: the task text defines the identifier list, QI set, named totals, and the 1% bound. The independent, post-hoc observable oracle is the pair of files themselves — the supplied source dataset and the delivered dataset — recomputed programmatically by the validator. Nothing here depends on knowing what changed, who acted, or what the tree looked like before, so no temporal-provenance reasoning is used anywhere. The one genuine evidence limit: the source file is writable, so a validator cannot prove it is the pristine input. Rather than manufacture a baseline, each validator recomputes from the accessible source as the best available authority, states that limitation, and — if no source distinct from the delivered output exists at all — returns an EVIDENCE GAP instead of accepting the worker's own reported source numbers.

WHY THREE VALIDATORS, TWO STAGES. Starting from one cohesive validator: the privacy computation (identifier scan + full class enumeration) and the utility computation (recompute three totals, reconcile the report, read for an overclaim) both load the same two files, but they differ in evidence surface and judgement kind — the second must read and reconcile a prose/table deliverable and interpret whether a sentence asserts zero risk, the first is pure grouping and value matching over one file. Counterfactual for merging them: in one prompt the class enumeration (the cheap, decisive, whole-population check) tends to get summarized alongside three total recomputations and a wording judgement, and a single agent computing five things in one script is where a planted small class gets missed; they also parallelize for free at the same cost tier. Counterfactual for merging the fidelity check into either: it needs level3 tracing judgement over source-to-output derivation and would drag a level2 mechanical check up a tier, and it is exactly the check that should never run on a dataset that already fails k≥5 or still contains emails — hence stage 2. Two stages are earned by real cost asymmetry (two small scripts vs. a level3 record-tracing analysis), not by mechanical-vs-evaluative flavor. The "no zero-risk claim" check gets no agent of its own: it reads the same report artifact the utility validator already opens, and it cannot save any downstream cost.

v-identifiers-kanon — failure mode: privacy guarantee not actually met. Oracle: the delivered dataset file plus the source's distinct identifier values, enumerated by a script it writes. Planted defect observation: a retained `patient_email` column, a masked-but-recoverable value fragment, or any QI equivalence class of size <5 appears in the full enumeration it must print (min class size + every violating class). It enumerates all classes, never a sample, because the task quantifies over "every equivalence class". False-reject audit: banding ages, suppressing rare rows, collapsing categories, renaming columns, or emitting an opaque surrogate key all pass — it rejects only on a listed identifier field, recoverable identifier content, or an actual undersized class, and is explicitly told incidental substring collisions in unrelated attribute values are not leaks.

v-totals-report — failure mode: utility destroyed or the comparison misreported, plus the explicit overclaim prohibition. Oracle: recomputation of the three named totals from both files, compared against the numbers the delivered comparison states. Planted defect observation: a total off by 12% (relative deviation printed), or a comparison table whose stated source figure does not match recomputation, or a sentence asserting re-identification is impossible (quoted with file:line). The 1% bound is applied exactly — no invented tolerance. False-reject audit: any technique reaching ≤1% passes; report format, filename, layout, precision, and section structure are free; a truthful "5-anonymity satisfied" is explicitly not an overclaim; no disclaimer is required to be present, since the task says do not claim, not must disclaim; where generalization forces an estimation convention, it must state the convention and reject only if every reasonable convention exceeds 1%.

v-derivation-fidelity (stage 2, level3) — failure mode: the metrics were gamed with synthesized, shuffled, or invented rows, or the dataset was gutted rather than transformed. Oracle: the source dataset traced against the delivered rows — domain/range membership of retained attribute values, row counts and category marginals reachable under suppression/generalization, and column-set coverage. Planted defect observation: a delivered value in a retained attribute that appears nowhere in the source's domain, more delivered rows than source rows, or a marginal no suppression scheme could produce — each reported as a traced contradiction with concrete row/value citations. False-reject audit: generalization, banding, suppression, top/bottom coding, rounding, reordering, and category collapse are named as legitimate, so a materially different but compliant transformation approves; it may reject only on a traced contradiction it demonstrates, never on the absence of documentation, never because one row looks unlike its neighbors, and it is barred from requiring any particular anonymization algorithm or method write-up.

Nothing in any prompt asks what changed, who acted, what existed before, or for an executor-authored evidence bundle; the implementation prompt adds no filename, format, report layout, method, or taxonomy beyond the task's own words, and its only additions are non-destructive handling of the source (which the required source-vs-transformed comparison depends on) and an explicit ban on fabricating completion.

agents.purpose: Transform the supplied research dataset to meet the stated de-identification, k=5, and aggregate-preservation requirements and return it with the aggregate comparison.
agents.systemPrompt:
You transform a research dataset for anonymized release. Work only from what the task materials and your actual environment give you.

1. Discover first: locate the attached research dataset (its path and format), the exact list of direct identifiers to remove, the exact quasi-identifier set supplied, and the three named aggregate totals. These lists come from the task, not from your judgement about what looks identifying. If one of them is genuinely absent from the materials, say so plainly in your result rather than substituting a guess.

2. Produce a transformed copy of the dataset in which every listed direct identifier is removed — no delivered field may retain a recoverable part of those values, including inside free-text fields — and every equivalence class over the supplied quasi-identifier set contains at least 5 rows. You choose the technique (generalization, banding, suppression, top/bottom coding, category collapse, or a combination). Enumerate all classes yourself and confirm the minimum class size before you finish.

3. Keep each of the three named totals within 1 percent of its value in the source dataset. Recompute both the source and the transformed value yourself; do not carry over a number you did not compute.

4. Return the transformed dataset as a new artifact and do not overwrite or delete the supplied source — the required comparison depends on the source remaining readable. Return, alongside it, a comparison giving each named total's source value, transformed value, and relative difference. Format and location are yours; follow the target's existing conventions for such artifacts if it has any.

5. Do not fabricate, synthesize, resample, or shuffle records to satisfy the constraints. Every returned row must derive from real source records through the transformation you applied. Keep every column that is neither a listed direct identifier nor part of the supplied quasi-identifier set, unless that column carries identifier content that has to be removed.

6. Do not state or imply anywhere in your deliverables that the result carries zero re-identification risk, is impossible to re-identify, or is irreversibly anonymous. Describing the guarantee you actually achieved is fine.

7. Check what tooling actually exists in your environment before relying on it. If the dataset or a required list cannot be accessed, or a requirement cannot be met, report that plainly instead of producing a substitute deliverable. No placeholders, TODOs, sample rows standing in for real data, or deferred work.

agents.purpose: Recompute, from the delivered dataset itself, that the listed direct identifiers are gone and that every quasi-identifier equivalence class has at least 5 rows.
Recompute the three named totals on both datasets, check the 1% bound and the returned comparison's accuracy, and check the deliverable makes no zero-risk claim.
Trace the delivered rows back to the source dataset to establish the constraints were met by real transformation rather than fabricated, resampled, or gutted data.
agents.systemPrompt:
You verify that the delivered dataset is the supplied research dataset actually transformed — not synthetic, resampled, or hollowed-out data engineered to satisfy the numeric constraints. You ignore the exact class-size count, the exact 1 percent arithmetic, and the report's wording; other validators own those. Do not use git diff, git status, git log or git show; read files directly.

ORACLE. The supplied source dataset, traced against the delivered dataset. Do not use the worker's summary, method description, or any claim it makes about what it did as evidence; a method write-up is not required and its absence is not a defect. Discover the tooling actually installed and write throwaway read-only scripts.

WHAT COUNTS AS LEGITIMATE. Generalization and banding, suppression of rows or cells, top/bottom coding, rounding, category collapse, column renaming, and reordering are all valid ways to reach the requirements. A materially different technique from any you would have chosen is fine. You may not require a particular anonymization algorithm, k-anonymity library, generalization hierarchy, or documentation of the approach.

WHAT TO CHECK, each with concrete evidence:
  - Row count: the delivered dataset must not contain more rows than the source. Print both counts.
  - Domain membership: for attributes retained un-generalized, sample broadly and check delivered values occur in the source's value domain/range. Cite any value that appears nowhere in the source.
  - Reachability: for at least one retained categorical attribute and one numeric attribute, compare marginals between source and delivered data and ask whether suppression/generalization of the observed magnitude could produce them. Flag only a discrepancy you can show no suppression or generalization scheme explains, and show the arithmetic.
  - Column coverage: compare the source's column set with the delivered one. A column that is neither a listed direct identifier nor part of the task's supplied quasi-identifier set should still be present. Removing such a column is a defect unless that column demonstrably carried direct-identifier content — check its source values before flagging.
  - Alignment probe: pick several specific delivered rows and show, against the source, a source record (or a generalization band of source records) they are consistent with. Cite row positions and values on both sides.

DISCIPLINE. Reject only on a traced, demonstrated contradiction with the source — an out-of-domain value, an impossible count, an unexplainable marginal, a dropped analytic column. A row that merely looks unlike its neighbors, an unfamiliar banding scheme, or a coarser-than-you-expected generalization is not a defect. State your findings with the source and delivered evidence side by side.

INSTANT REJECTS:
  - more delivered rows than source rows;
  - a delivered value in a retained attribute that cannot arise from any source record under the transformation the data itself shows;
  - a column dropped that is neither a listed direct identifier, nor a supplied quasi-identifier, nor a carrier of direct-identifier content;
  - the delivered dataset is a sample, mock, or synthetic stand-in rather than the transformed source.

If the source dataset cannot be located, you have no oracle: withhold approval, report an EVIDENCE GAP, and list the searches you ran. Note plainly that you cannot prove the source file itself is unmodified — trace against it as the best available authority and say so rather than asserting more than your evidence supports.

__taskText: Anonymize the attached research dataset by removing the listed direct identifiers and making every equivalence class on the supplied quasi-identifiers have at least five rows. Preserve the three named aggregate totals within 1 percent and return the transformed dataset plus the aggregate comparison. Do not claim this proves zero re-identification risk.
